newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTORCYCLING-JACQUE HOPES TO STEAL SHOW FROM DOOHAN.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-JACQUE HOPES TO STEAL SHOW FROM DOOHAN.

text.p: Michael Doohan is such a hot favourite to win his fifth victory of the season in Sunday's French motorcycling Grand Prix at Le Castellet that the local crowd will for once turn to the 250cc race section, hoping for a victory by Frenchman Olivier Jacque.

The Australian, a comfortable winner here last year, comes into the French leg of the 500cc world championship with an even better record than last season, having won four of the five races held this year.
The reigning world champion scored his 38th Grand Prix victory in Austria last week, a success record bettered only by Giacomo Agostini, who won 68 races in his career.
On Sunday, only his Honda team mates Alex Criville of Spain and Japanese Taddy Okada seem capable of upsetting Doohan.
Criville, who fell here last year after posting the fastest qualifying time, won the Spanish Grand Prix this season, the only race Doohan did not take.
For the French public, the 250cc race will be the highlight event of the weekend, with local hero Jacque hoping to confirm his victory in Austria.
"I could not dream of starting the French Grand Prix in better conditions. I know the track perfectly well," he said.
Jacque had to wait for the last race of the 1996 season in Brazil to score his first Grand Prix win. He made it two last week after overtaking Germany's Ralf Waldmann on the last lap.
"Beware of (Max) Biaggi," said the Honda rider. The Italian world champion leads the world championship standings with a nine-point lead over Waldmann and 30 over Jacque.
In the 125 cc section, Japan's Noburu Ueda, riding a Honda, and Italy's Valentino Rossi, winner this season in Malaysia, Spain and Italy, will be the favourites.
